prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The central woman remains the nearest large person, roughly 0.4–0.8 m in front of the camera wearer, while the standing people and mannequins behind her appear about 1.5–3 m away; her hands and the dark fabric or bag at the bottom are especially close, approximately 0.2–0.5 m. She is centered or slightly right of center and faces generally toward the camera, with her head angled downward or sideways; background figures stand to her left and right, partly behind her, and are mutually separated by roughly 0.5–1.5 m. Across the five frames, her apparent distance changes little, though lateral camera or body motion shifts her from center-left to center-right and changes which background people are visible; the foreground hand or fabric intermittently rises into the lower edge. The depth map makes foreground-background layering and arm-reach regions clearer than RGB, but facial depth is clipped to near-white, thin structures merge, and several background surfaces or people have weak or inconsistent depth, so metre estimates are approximate.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map consistently isolates the central woman as the dominant foreground person and separates several other people or mannequin-like figures along the left and right background, clarifying overlaps that are difficult to parse in RGB. The central mask occupies most of the middle and lower image, placing her within roughly 0.5–1 m, while the smaller masks near the edges and behind her are plausibly around 1.5–3 m away; side figures appear roughly 0.5–2 m laterally from her in scene space. Across the strip, the central person shifts laterally and increasingly occludes or reveals people behind her, while some peripheral figures enter or leave the cropped field of view; a narrow tie-like mask appears over her torso in one frame. This map is unreliable for object identity and geometry: nearly everything is labelled “person,” parts of the central body contain holes or merged regions, the close fabric or bag is absorbed into her mask, and edge masks are truncated or fragmented.
descriptions.pose: The pose map shows the central woman’s upper-body and hand configuration: her torso is close and approximately frontal, her arms descend toward the foreground surface, and the magenta hand keypoints lie near the bottom center or lower left, within about 0.2–0.6 m of the camera wearer. Her head keypoints remain above the torso, but face direction and gaze toward the camera cannot be established reliably because facial landmarks are sparse and her face is partly cropped or obscured by glasses and head angle; background people are mostly not reconstructed. From left to right, the detected body shifts across the frame and becomes increasingly incomplete, while the detected hand moves from lower left toward center and then right, consistent with lateral viewpoint or body motion rather than a clear approach or retreat. Pose reveals joint and hand placement that RGB alone makes hard to separate from dark clothing and fabric, but it is highly unreliable here: limbs disappear, joints connect implausibly, isolated hands lack bodies, and the fifth frame contains only a partial arm-hand skeleton near the right side.
